title: Initiative chunking and deferred-deliverable protocol for multi-cycle launches
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Establish a repeatable protocol for slicing large initiatives into launchable chunks and defining a formal deferred-deliverable process to protect throughput during unplanned on-call/workload disruptions. This ticket defines rules for chunk sizing, acceptance criteria for partial launches, staffing guards, and the de-scope scoring rubric used during cycle triage.
acceptance_criteria: A documented chunking template exists with max chunk size, typical vertical slice contents, and required cross-team touchpoints
A de-scope rubric (scoring matrix) is published and adopted by PMs/EMs — includes customer impact, implementation risk, and dependency cost
On-call buffer and surge lane allocation rules are defined and communicated to Eng leads and applied to Cycle 45 staffing plans
Runbook for executing deferred-deliverable flows (who owns deferred items, retention period, and handoff steps) is created and linked
Two pilot initiatives use the protocol in Cycle 45 and provide retrospective notes
decision_log: 2026-02-16: Decided max chunk should aim for <= 4 engineer-weeks of work to keep rollout predictable. Trade-off: smaller chunks increase coordination overhead but reduce single-point failure risk.

2026-02-20: Chose customer-impact-first scoring weight (40%) for de-scope rubric, then delivery complexity (30%), observability cost (15%), cross-team dependency risk (15%). Rationale: maintain perceived user value while minimizing operational surprises.
2026-02-25: Allocated a 10% on-call buffer and 15% surge lane capacity per initiative for Cycle 45; larger launches may request variance via product council.

2026-02-28: Decided deferred deliverables will be retained in the originating initiative backlog with a defined triage owner; deferred items older than 2 cycles will require re-evaluation by PM and EMs before re-commitment.
comments: 2026-02-17 (Marco): Draft chunking template uploaded to Drive -> /Drive/Redwood/Product/Cycle_Flex/chunking-template-v1.md
2026-02-18 (Lina Rodriguez - Eng Lead): Concern about cross-team API dependencies; recommended adding an API compatibility gate as a required artifact for chunks dependent on other services.
2026-02-19 (Samir Patel - Design): Proposed minimum UX acceptance criteria for partial launches: flow A must be end-to-end and have metrics tracked in Console dashboards.
2026-02-22 (PM Council Review): Approved rubric with one modification: increase weight on observability cost when the initiative includes runtime changes (kernels, batching).
2026-02-26 (Marco): Created ENG spike to prototype chunk rollout automation: ENG-42333 (prefill feature flags and rollout canary steps).
2026-03-01 (Aisha): Ready for two pilot teams (Optimize and Console) to trial; scheduling kickoff with EMs week of 2026-03-08.
notes: Pilot approach: two initiatives (Optimize: quantization recommendations; Console: rollout UX for rollouts) will break into 3 chunks each. Each chunk must include: acceptance tests, monitoring dashboard, rollback steps, and a release checklist. EMs should reserve the on-call buffer immediately in Cycle 45 planning sheets. Post-pilot retrospective due by 2026-03-30 to update runbook and rubric weights.
